newsitem.title: UK: Chernobyl gets $150 million safety grant.
newsitem.headline: Chernobyl gets $150 million safety grant.

text.p: Chernobyl nuclear power plant has been awarded 118 million European Currency Units ($151 million) in aid for decomissioning and safety measures, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development said on Tuesday.
The funds are being provided by the Nuclear Safety Account, an EBRD administered fund financed which is financed by 15 countries for closing highly dangerous reactors in Central and Eastern Europe.

"This is a very concrete step by the Ukrainian government and the international community towards the closure of Chernobyl," said EBRD deputy vice-president, Joachim Jahnke told a signing ceremony for the grant in London.
The money will be used to establish a temporary spent nuclear fuel facility to store assemblies from the plant, liquid waste treatment operations and safety measures at the number three reactor.

The grant is part of a $350 million provision by the NSA and other donors towards the decomissioning of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant, which was the site of the world's worst nuclear accident 10 years ago.
Kiev has agreed to close the plant by 2000 in return for $3.0 billion in grants and funding from the Group of Seven leading industrialised nations.

"We are all under a tight schedule and this is an important development and strong indication of the resolve of all parties to reach this vital goal," Jahnke said, referring to the planned closure of Chernobyl by the year 2000.

Ukraine is heavily dependent on nuclear power for electricity and currently imports two thirds of its energy requirements from Russia, which no longer provides heavily subsidised oil for the countries of the former Soviet Union.
The EBRD is also funding a panel of experts to examine the feasibility of getting two reactors up and running in time for the closure of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant.
